subject: Career
title: The Recency Bias in Hiring
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Recency Bias in Hiring.

hook.text: The last resume a recruiter reads often gets an unfair advantage. That's recency bias.

buildup.text: Hiring decisions are influenced by memory. Recent applications are more vivid.

discovery.text: Applying early in a posting's life means your resume might be forgotten by decision day.

twist.text: Applying too late means the shortlist may already be full. Timing is a real strategy.

climax.text: The sweet spot: apply within the first week, then follow up right before interviews start.

punchline.text: When you apply matters almost as much as what.

quiz.question: What is recency bias in hiring?
options: Recent applications are remembered more vividly

details.summary: Recency bias causes hiring managers to weight your most recent role far more heavily than your earlier career. This means your current or most recent position must strongly align with the target role, even if older experience is equally or more relevant.
details.whyItMatters: If your most recent role appears unrelated to the target position, recency bias may override ten years of relevant prior experience. Strategic framing of your current role addresses this.
takeaways: Invest the most resume space in your most recent and relevant roles
Frame your current role to emphasize transferable skills to the target position
Older but relevant experience needs explicit connection to the role

faq.question: How do you overcome recency bias when your most recent role is not the most relevant?
faq.answer: Reframe your recent role's bullet points to emphasize transferable skills that align with the target. Lead with a strong professional summary that bridges your recent experience to the desired role. Consider whether a functional or combination format might better serve your candidacy.

faq.question: Should you reduce the content about your most recent role if it is not relevant?
faq.answer: No. Reducing recent role content creates a gap that looks worse than misalignment. Instead, increase the relevance of your recent role's description by highlighting transferable aspects. Then expand the content for your most relevant older role to signal its importance.
